title: I am seeing what appears to be a bug with MD LiveSync 2.2.2 in Unreal Engine 5.7.
content:
Environment:  
\- UE 5.7  
\- MD LiveSync 2.2.2  
\- Marvelous Designer 2025.2.231  
  
Issue:  
\- LiveSync connection status is green in Unreal  
\- Update starts, stops around 50%, then goes to around 80%  
\- Nothing is imported into Unreal

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Morisanpei,This was a mistake on our end. MD LiveSync version 2.2.2 was published prematurely; it is a newer version meant for Marvelous Designer 2026.0, which has not been released yet. Could you roll it back to 2.2.1 by following these steps?1. .Go to our LiveSync version archive and download version 2.2.1 for UE 5.7. https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4d651a5d6c9f434fad4c8b5adde39798 Next, navigate to the UE 5.7 installation directory (e.g., C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.7\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace).3. Then, Delete version 2.2.2, then unzip the downloaded 2.2.1 package and place the entire 'CLOLiveSync' folder into that directory.Let me know if this works for you!Once Marvelous Designer 2026.0 is released, please make sure to remove version 2.2.1 and download version 2.2.2 directly from the Epic Games Launcher. 🙂Thank you!Best regards,Bryan
content_description: Provide troubleshooting guidance for resolving incomplete Marvelous Designer asset imports during LiveSync integration with Unreal Engine 5.7.

title: Accidental changes and synchronization
content:
I don't think there is a single MD user that doesn't suffer from the constant unintended synchronization during accidental clicks or moves.

Since you don't have mercy on us giving us a button to allow us to invoke Synchronization ourselves. Maybe it is possible to at least allow us to abort synchronization and undo the last change when we would press ESC during synchronization? I think this shouldn't mess up any workflows. And it would contribute to my mental health enormously. MD is a great program but it doesn't seem to give any consideration to how frustrating it can be to make simple changes which lead to lengthy calculations where you deactivated everything not needed and still it takes forever for simple things. Tho i admit maybe you can't do anything about those waiting times. But i would think at least it should be possible to be able to stop calculations for unwanted changes and revert them faster than waiting for them to finish and then wait again for undoing them.

Please have mercy on our broken souls ;), thank you.
content_description: This page advocates for improved user control in MD software by enabling users to abort unintended synchronizations and quickly undo changes to reduce frustration and enhance workflow efficiency.

title: One CPU core constantly used even when MD minimized and no project loaded
content:
Why is MD exhausting constantly one CPU core ?

Even when MD is minimized and doesn't even have any Project open / any patterns.

What is that program constantly doing in the background ?

I am on the latest Version 2025.2.255

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Brewka,While usually programs use PC resources like the CPU to keep the program open and running, if it is consuming more resources than it has in past builds that would be frustrating and could be a bug. Don't post here but please send us a support ticket with more specifics of what you are seeing: especially pictures, screenshots/recordings so we can better understand this issue. Since its Marvelous Designer doing this - send us the information here: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/615a09d19372422682cb25d673b366c6 your message please let us know the defaults of the device, but also try to include any possible outliers like: if you have overlclocked your PC or are running non-default settings that might affect your recource allocation. The more you are able to share the better, so we can try to replicate it on our end and find a solution!🙏🏻
Reply 1: It seems the constant processing on one CPU core does not occur anymore in the 2026 update :)
content_description: To explain why MD continuously uses one CPU core even when minimized and idle, and to clarify what background processes it performs in the latest version 2025.2.255.

content:

Unreal Engine 5.7.4

Livesync 2.2.2

Marvelous Designer 2025.2.143

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi coj,The issue could occur when a certain part of a garment has too many meshes (e.g., seamlines or topstitches). I'd like to examine the CLO project file you are using to reproduce the issue on my end and provide you with a workaround. Could you please submit a support ticket, include the .zprj file, and mention my name in the ticket?Best regards,Bryan

Comment 2: As far as I know, when the Unreal engine is updated, it takes time to be compatible with CLO3D and Livesync.Even if it's a little cumbersome, why don't you use Unreal Engine in 5.6 version?LiveSync 2 version archive – Help Center - CONNECT
Reply 1: My metahuman was made in 5.7 and there's no way to port it to 5.6 unfortunately. I also tried to manually adjust the sliders the same way I did in 5.7 but the results are totally different.
